try.instruction: Build a full sentence. Start with The girls. One word stays.

scene.text: Two girls / clap their hands / now

try.answerText: The girls are clapping their hands.

try.hint: Two girls go with are. Then add the action.
try.explanation: Use are with the girls. Clapping tells what they are doing now.

try.hint: Mia is one person. Use is and her.
try.explanation: One girl goes with is. Her hands are Mia's hands.

try.answerText: The girls are facing each other.

try.hint: Check the word just after the girls.
try.explanation: Use are for two girls. Facing each other means each girl faces the other girl.

try.instruction: Build a full sentence. Start with I. One word stays.

scene.text: You help the teacher / mop the floor
scene.heading: Read the situation

try.answerText: I help by mopping the floor.
try.spokenQuestion: You mop the floor to help the teacher. How do you help?

try.explanation: By mopping tells how you help. Use mopping after by.

try.prompt: Make this a sentence about how you help.

scene.text: I clean the floor.

try.answerText: I help by cleaning the floor.

try.explanation: I clean the floor names an action. I help by cleaning the floor tells how you help.

try.hint: The action after by needs an ing ending.
try.explanation: Use giving after by. We means you and Jo together.

scene.text: You help the teacher / give books to children
scene.heading: Read the situation

say.answerText: I help by giving books to children.

concepts.title: Put two actions in one sentence

try.prompt: What do they do? Say both actions.
try.instruction: Build a full sentence. Start with They. One word stays.

scene.text: Story parents / cook food + wash clothes
scene.heading: Read the situation

try.answerText: They cook food and wash clothes.
try.spokenQuestion: In this story, two parents cook food. They wash clothes too. Tell me both actions in one sentence.
try.hint: Both actions happen. Join them with and.
try.explanation: And joins two things they do. Or would give a choice between the actions.

try.prompt: Join the two sentences. Say They only once.
try.instruction: Build a full sentence. Start with They. One word stays.

scene.text: They take Leo to school. They wash clothes.
scene.heading: Two short sentences

try.answerText: They take Leo to school and wash clothes.
try.spokenQuestion: These story parents take Leo to school. They wash clothes too. Join the two sentences and say they only once.
try.hint: Keep both actions. Put and between them.
try.explanation: They can name the parents once. And joins taking Leo to school with washing clothes.

try.prompt: Both actions happen. Fix one word.
try.instruction: Tap the mistake. Choose a word.

scene.text: Story parents / every day: cook food + check homework
scene.heading: Read the situation

try.answerText: They cook food and check homework.
try.spokenQuestion: The story parents do both jobs every day: cooking food, checking homework. Fix the word that joins the jobs.
try.hint: Choose the joining word for two things that both happen.
try.explanation: And says they do both jobs. Or does not clearly say that they do both.

say.prompt: What do they do? Say both actions.

scene.text: Story parents / cook food + check homework

The parents cook food and check homework.

scene.heading: Read the situation

The parents wash clothes and cook food.
